title: Accelerating Nested Virtualization with HyperTurtle
problem: Nested virtualization (running virtual machines within virtual machines) incurs significant performance overhead due to repeated VM exits and trap handling. This overhead limits practical adoption in cloud and container environments.
motivation: Nested virtualization enables critical use cases including cloud migration, security isolation, and container consolidation, but performance degradation must be addressed.
method: HyperTurtle provides hardware-level acceleration for nested VM operations through optimized exit handling and reduced transition latency. The system likely streamlines nested VM entry/exit paths and context switching to minimize overhead from VM traps and privilege level transitions.
key_novelty: Hardware-accelerated optimization specifically targeting the performance bottlenecks of nested virtualization rather than treating it as a simple iteration of single-level virtualization.
contributions: HyperTurtle system architecture for accelerating nested virtualization
Optimizations reducing nested VM exit latency and transition overhead
Performance evaluation demonstrating speedup of nested VM workloads
